text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: P1 page - Streaming tail latency spike in eu-west2. Symptoms: elevated p95/p99 for stream endpoints, client streaming stalls. Pager: @oncall-anne. Auto-escalate to netops & sre.
oncall-anne: on it. seeing alerts: p95=1.1s -> 3.4s, p99=2.7s -> 18s for streaming-chunk API. Any customer reports?
support-raj: 7 customer tickets opened in last 25m, 3_high severity. Postgres-backend metrics look normal.
netops-jay: I'm seeing increased SYN retransmits across nat-gw-a in eu-west2, conntrack counts spiking. Packet loss ~0.6% on egress path, RTT for TLS handshake increased.
sre-miguel: can you dump conntrack / ephemeral port usage on nat-gw-a? also need streaming proxy logs for stalls.
netops-jay: running: `ssh nat-gw-a 'sudo conntrack -L | wc -l'` -> 168,900 entries (cap 200k). ephemeral ports used ~95% on nat-gw-a.
eng-runtime-lee: streaming proxies are seeing TLS handshake failures with ECONNRESET and increased handoff timeouts. KV cache hits unchanged so not app-level.
sre-miguel: hypothesis: NAT ephemeral port exhaustion causing flow teardown and TLS handshake retries -> tail latency. Possible mixing of long-lived streaming sockets with short-lived outbound requests.
oncall-anne: mitigation options: 1) reroute subset of traffic to nat-gw-b, 2) expand nat pool / ephemeral port range, 3) apply aggressive SYN retries backoff. Which is fastest?
netops-jay: reroute is fastest. Preparing traffic shift for 10% -> 40% to gw-b. Command: `controlplane route shift --region eu-west2 --from nat-gw-a --to nat-gw-b --percent 40 --dry-run` then remove dry-run.
sre-miguel: also bump conntrack_max and net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range on nat-gw-a as medium-term: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=400000` and `sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range='15000 61000'` - but do after reroute to avoid transient overload.
netops-jay: executing reroute now. `controlplane route shift ... --percent 40`
netops-jay: :white_check_mark: shift applied. monitoring.
oncall-anne: switching some streaming-prefixed routes to gw-c for long-lived flows only to reduce ephemeral churn.
eng-runtime-lee: applying streaming route rule change: `rbctl modify-route streaming --egress gw-c --sticky-connections true` -> applied.
support-raj: customer ticket update: told customers we're investigating and applied temporary reroute, asked to reopen if issues persist.
10m later...
netops-jay: conntrack on nat-gw-a falling: 168900 -> 112300. ephemeral usage down to 62%. SYN retransmit rate dropping.
sre-miguel: p95/p99 trending: p95 3.4s -> 1.2s, p99 18s -> 3.6s. Streaming stalls count decreased ~78%.
product-olivia: any user-visible regressions from reroute? region-specific customers?
support-raj: no new high-sev tickets in last 12m. some low-level reconnects but overall fewer complaints.
oncall-anne: marking immediate mitigation as successful. Next: postmortem tasks - confirm root cause, apply conntrack increase permanently, revisit NAT design (elastic ephemeral pools), and add early-warning for ephemeral exhaustion.
eng-runtime-lee: follow-up: add connection reuse for internal calls from streaming workers to reduce churn, and add streaming-specific egress pools.
sre-miguel: root cause note: NAT ephemeral exhaustion + short connection churn + DNS failover amplification led to burst of TLS handshakes. Plan: infra change + runtime connection pooling.
netops-jay: will file infra task to add nat autoscaling and monitoring for ip_local_port_range thresholds.
oncall-anne: closing page. will create incident report and customer comms draft. :white_check_mark:
incidents-bot: Incident resolved - status: mitigated. Please fill postmortem template: /wiki/incidents/postmortem-template
